models_evaluated: 16 published CKD/kidney failure risk prediction models (7 general population, 9 type 2 diabetes)

links.outcome: Calibration of published kidney risk models on an external population
links.effect: Severe miscalibration for many models; most substantially overpredicted CKD risk while underpredicting kidney failure risk, so recalibration is warranted before clinical application.
links.quote: Calibration performance was frequently suboptimal; most models substantially overpredicted CKD risk while underpredicting kidney failure risk, indicating that recalibration is warranted prior to clinical application.

links.outcome: Model discrimination across subgroups (age, sex, ethnicity, diabetes, hypertension)
links.effect: Discriminative performance was poorer for people with diabetes or hypertension.
links.quote: Discriminative performance was poorer for people with diabetes or hypertension.

screen.reason: The study conducts a comparative external validation of 16 existing clinical risk prediction models across 0.5 million UK Biobank participants, evaluating discrimination, calibration, and subgroup performance (fairness/generalizability) without directly testing a specific intervention or deployment safeguard practice.
